precepts.text: When your coworkers wondering why this brother don't murmur with them and don't ever work the Sabbath: keep therefore and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people. The other nations are expecting you to be that greedy individual that lacks integrity, but we give them this right here.
precepts.point: This is how they infiltrate organizations, through money. Organizations fail because of money: they infiltrate, they come in, offer money, and they give up their organization. That mean they lacked integrity; they let money come in and dictate and control the movement. That ain't happening here.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.why:
Judas is the character we are not to have. “This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag.” He walked with Christ and saw many miracles, and still betrayed the savior and everybody around him. Money was his root and his god: greed. That is how they infiltrate organizations: they come in and offer money, and a people lacking integrity gives up the organization and lets money dictate and control the movement. That ain't happening here.

Israel is to give the nations the opposite: “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” Keeping the law is our wisdom, and it is seen.

When your coworkers wonder why this brother doesn't murmur with them and never works the Sabbath, that is the nations seeing the statutes kept. The other nations are expecting you to be that greedy individual that lacks integrity, a Judas who can be bought. We give them this right here: character and integrity, the hidden strength behind wisdom.

precepts.text: Judas complained about Mary's ointment not because he cared for the poor but because he was a thief with the bag. And because many Jews believed on Jesus by reason of Lazarus, the chief priests consulted to put Lazarus also to death. That is next-level evil, and it is what they will do to us.
precepts.point: That is the church blitz in the Bible. Our own people will persecute the prophets who bring them the truth, in their churches, which is where we have to go. We arrive with the same Bible they have and they put hands on us and pull guns, with the love of Jesus.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
This shows how evil they are. Six days before the passover Christ came to Bethany, “where Lazarus was which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.” At the supper Mary took “a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair”.

Judas Iscariot complained: “Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor? This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein.” Christ answered, “Let her alone: against the day of my burying hath she kept this. For the poor always ye have with you; but me ye have not always.”

“Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.” In the chapter before, the Pharisees had already said, we have to kill this man because he does many miracles and Rome is going to take away our place.

Now: “But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death; Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.” Christ raised Lazarus out of the grave, and they said it is not just Christ we have to kill; we have to kill the one he raised from the dead too. That is next-level evil.

And that is what they will do to us. Because by reason of the truth many believe on Christ, they will seek to put us to death, the same as “some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues”.

precepts.text: A voice came from heaven, and the people that stood by said it thundered; Christ said the voice came not because of him but for their sakes, showing the thunder was the Most High speaking.
precepts.point: The Most High sent out arrows and lightning and scattered his enemies, and the channels of the sea and the foundations of the world were discovered at the rebuking of the Lord, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils. His power over creation is total.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
Christ prayed, “Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again. The people therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it thundered: others said, An angel spake to him. Jesus answered and said, This voice came not because of me, but for your sakes.”

The people heard the voice of the Father and called it thunder. That shows the thunder is the Most High speaking, just as David sang, “The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice.” We hear it, but we cannot comprehend it because we no longer have that spirit upon us.

precepts.text: He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, that they should not see nor understand and be converted; the eyes must first be converted before a man can see this truth.
precepts.point: I am a stranger in the earth; hide not Thy commandments from me. Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from Thy commandments. His testimonies are the delight of the servant and his counselors even when princes sit and speak against him.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” Our people's eyes are closed and shut to the truth of this Bible. “He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.”

The eyes must first be converted before a man can see this truth. The only way we will see it is if we keep the laws of the Most High; once we keep them our eyes start to open to the truth around us, to who we are, what is required of us, who our enemies are and who the other nations are. But you have to be converted in the laws first.

precepts.text: Christ quoted Isaiah: they could not believe because the Most High blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts.
precepts.point: The eyes of them that see shall not be dim and the ears of them that hear shall hearken; you will begin to see spiritually and hear with understanding. The heart of the rash shall understand knowledge and the stammering tongue shall speak plainly.

note.label: Isaiah 32: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness

precepts.why:
Christ quoted Isaiah on the eyes and ears. “But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him: That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled”. “Therefore they could not believe, because that Esaias said again, He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.”

They could not believe, because the Most High blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, just as Isaiah 6 said. So when Isaiah 32 says “the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken”, it is the turning of that blindness: you will begin to see spiritually and hear with understanding, and the heart that was hardened “shall understand knowledge”.

precepts.text: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.”

Much people came to the feast and cried out that he is the King of Israel. That multitude was Israel, and it is that same multitude the Pharisees are speaking of next when they say the world is gone after him. So the world in “God so loved the world” is that people, the ones who called him the King of Israel.

precepts.text: The Pharisees said, Behold, the world is gone after him, of that same multitude.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.”

The Pharisees said the world is gone after him, of that same multitude that took branches of palm trees and cried, “Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.” That multitude was the world. John's own gospel uses the word that way, so “God so loved the world” is speaking of that people, the same ones the serpent was lifted up for.

precepts.text: Much people of the Jews believed on Jesus after seeing Lazarus raised, but the chief priests consulted to put Lazarus also to death.
precepts.point: This five thousand disproves the Christian claim that the Jews all rejected Christ. He came unto his own, meaning the religious leaders, the builders, the chief priests and rulers whose job was to guide the nation, and only those upper echelons rejected him, while thousands of the people believed and were zealous of the law.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“Much people of the Jews” came to see Lazarus whom Christ had raised, “But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death; Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.”

The people believed; the chief priests plotted. That is the split: the ones who rejected Christ were the rulers, not the nation.

precepts.text: Many of the Jews believed on Jesus after seeing Lazarus, but the chief priests consulted to put Lazarus also to death, showing their wickedness against plain miracles.
precepts.point: The Pharisees were divided over Christ, some saying he is not of God because he healed on the Sabbath, others asking how a man that is a sinner could do such miracles. That same division will bring people out of the Christian church to examine the matter and repent based on our works.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
They had done this before. “Much people of the Jews” came to see Lazarus, “whom he had raised from the dead. But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death”.

Christ raised a man from the dead, and they consulted to put him back in the grave. Now a notable miracle has been done that they cannot deny, and instead of glorifying God they choose to threaten the disciples. It was never about the miracle but about losing their power and their seat of authority. Satan cannot cast out Satan, so they knew the miracle was of the Most High. You have to be that wicked to witness the great works and still plot against the men who did them. That level of hatred, envy and emulation is what the religious leaders had for the people.

precepts.text: Certain Greeks came up to worship at the feast, and the disciples carried their request to Christ.
precepts.point: The feast of dedication Christ kept in John 10 commemorates the Maccabees driving out the Greeks and rededicating the temple the Greeks had profaned. Christ would not turn around a few months later and accept those same Greeks.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
“And there were certain Greeks among them that came up to worship at the feast”. They came up to worship at the passover, and the disciples carried their request to Christ.

Devout Israelites came back to Jerusalem to keep the feasts no matter where they were scattered, so these certain Greeks were Israelites keeping the law, not heathen. They are the same as the Grecians of Acts 6: Israelites out of the Greek provinces called by the name of the land. Christ answered them with prophecy; a real Greek got a very different answer.

precepts.text: When the voice came from heaven, some said it thundered and others said an angel spake, two witness accounts of one event.
precepts.point: It was a caravan of men. Based on each man's account, one group heard the voice but saw no man, and another group saw the light but heard no voice, just as men running from the same scene report different pieces of it. There is no contradiction in the Bible.
precepts.why:
The same thing happened when Christ prayed, “Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.” One event, and two witness accounts: “The people therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it thundered: others said, An angel spake to him.”

Some heard thunder, others heard an angel, from the same voice. So with Saul's caravan: some heard a voice but saw no man, and some saw the light but heard no voice. Different men report different pieces of the same scene; that is not a contradiction.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: He said if one went unto them from the dead they will repent. “Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.” Christ had just raised Lazarus from the dead. “But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death”. You see how wicked these are? These are wicked as hell. One came back from the dead, and instead of repenting they wanted to kill him again.

“Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.” This is six days before the Passover, in Bethany. Everyone knew Lazarus was dead, so they came to see with their own eyes whether he was really alive.

“But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death”: black devils, going to kill Lazarus a second time. “Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.” Keep that in mind: many of the Jews believed on Christ because he raised Lazarus.

Then read on: “For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle. The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.” We are losing our following. What world went after Christ because of Lazarus? Were all nations there? Verse 11 tells you: many of the Jews went away and believed. So the Pharisees called the Jews the world. The cosmos. We are the world, and not the Michael Jackson song; the biblical world.

“Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him?” They followed Christ everywhere, like people do us, harassing. “Will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?”

Will he go and teach the scattered among the Gentiles? The Gentiles here are the dispersed: the word Gentiles here is Israelites. And the margin reads Greeks: it is the same word, Hellen, used for the Greeks in John 12:20. So Gentiles and Greeks are synonymous, used of the same people.

Other versions say it plainly: will he go to the dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks? Will he go where our people live scattered among the Greeks? Because the Greeks are the dispersion. The dispersion are called Greeks and Gentiles: the children of God scattered abroad.

“If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him”, and all men there is not all nations. “And the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” Then Caiaphas: “it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” One man dying for the people, by the prophecy of Daniel 9 and Isaiah 53.

“And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.”

That nation is Judah, the Jews. And the children of God scattered abroad are the Gentiles of John 7:35: the dispersed. So the Greeks who came to the feast are the children of God scattered abroad.

“They went both together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spake, that a great multitude both of the Jews and also of the Greeks believed. But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles”.

The Jews and the Greeks here were both Israelites, Greek speaking Jews and Jews alike, in the same synagogue. These are the same Greeks who came up to worship in John 12:20: Israelites scattered abroad who made the language, religion and worship of the Greeks their own, and so fell under the name Greeks, Hellenes.

“A certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek”.

Timothy’s father was a Greek: a pagan, but an Israelite too. The same kind of Greek as the ones in John 12:20.

“Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, And every one should leave his laws”. All become one people, all become Greeks, the way everyone in America becomes an American: Chinese American, Italian American, African American.

“Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” They changed their religion and worship and turned into Greeks: that is the primary meaning of Greeks. And the Greeks who came to worship at the feast had converted back to the customs of their forefathers.

Second Maccabees gives more detail about that consenting. “The king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God”: to force them to change their religion and worship into the Greek fashions and become Hellenized, assimilated.

“And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius”: polluted, not destroyed; it was destroyed in the time of the Romans. Jupiter is Zeus. Then verse 6: “Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.”

We were forbidden to profess ourselves Jews. We became Greeks, willingly or by force. As the years went on and Rome came to power, Jews born and raised in those customs grew up as Greeks, with Greek names and Greek ways, but they were still our people. That is who Paul was speaking of, and who the Jews meant in John 7:35: the dispersion among the Gentiles, our people called Greeks or Gentiles.

“Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass’s colt. These things understood not his disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.”

That’s excellent: these things understood not his disciples at the first. It was afterwards that they said, I remember that in Zechariah, he fits that. That’s how Apollos proved it to the people: remember when he came on the foal of an ass? That’s what it said in Zechariah.

Though one rose from the dead, they would not be persuaded. When Christ raised Lazarus, what was the plot? “Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead. But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death”: they would put him to death. That’s how wicked these Israelites were. “Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.” These dudes were so wicked: a man was raised from the dead and they plotted to kill that man. We got to put that dude back to death? The hell is this.

“While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light.” Christ “had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him”: our people did not believe, “That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled”. “He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted”, converted by Christ.

“These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him.” Isaiah saw the glory of Christ and spoke of Christ. That is not hard reading comprehension. And the same way Isaiah prophesied the eyes of the Pharisees would be blinded, today many of our people’s eyes are going to be blinded to what is brought out here.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
“Yet a little while is the light with you. Walk while ye have the light”: walk while you have me, “lest darkness come upon you”, lest you go into sin, “for he that walketh in darkness knoweth not whither he goeth.” He’s lost.

“While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light.” We are the children of light. We throw light here; we don’t do dark moons. You dark moon, you’re a child of darkness: that’s what the Bible says. Don’t get mad at me; get mad at your God that made you to be rebellious. We are the children of Christ, coming from Christ, the alpha of light, the main one. As long as he was in the world he was the light; once he died, what happened?

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: Here’s the evidence that they won’t be persuaded though one rose from the dead. “Then Jesus six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.” Remember in history, Christ raised Lazarus from the dead.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
“Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead. But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death”. Do y’all see that? They wanted to put Lazarus to death, “Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.”

Then the people “took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord”, and Jesus sat on a young ass, as it is written, “Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass’s colt.” “The people therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of his grave, and raised him from the dead, bare record.”

When Lazarus was raised from the dead, those same wicked scribes and Pharisees plotted and planned to put Lazarus to death. That’s why Abraham said to the rich man, if they don’t believe Moses and the prophets, they won’t believe though one rose from the dead.

Our forefathers understood who the world was. They were not colorblind.

“Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there”. Christ raised Lazarus from the dead, “Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.”

“For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle. The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.” What did the Pharisees call the Jews? The world. They understood who the world was.

“And there were certain Greeks”. Those Greeks were among the Jews counted as the world. But Christianity wants you colorblind to your own race, to forget who you are as a nation, and to look at them as your god whose ways are pure while you are nothing but a gentile who should be happy they took you from the shores of Africa and civilized you. Christianity programmed our people to demonize our own heritage and give up our name, identity and tongue to fit into their squares, circles and triangles, to hate ourselves and how we look.

Back to John to weigh it again: “That the saying of” Isaiah “the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, Lord, who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?” “He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.” The I that should heal them is the Lord, Christ. That’s what Isaiah saw.

“These things said” Isaiah “when he saw his glory, and spake of him”: he spoke of Christ. That is who Isaiah was speaking about in Isaiah 6. He saw the Lord of hosts, he saw the King, and that was Christ: he saw him in his eternal form in the heavens. Remember Corinthians 15: the last Adam is the Lord from heaven.

When the spirit opened this up, it was plain: the Lord we read about right through the scripture is Christ on the throne. It is not until the end that we see the Father, in Daniel 7. That’s Christ’s Father.

“The people therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of his grave, and raised him from the dead, bare record. For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle. The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.”

The world that went after Christ is Israel. There are many other scriptures that explain that, but these two scriptures go right to the point: the world God so loved is the nation of Israel.

“The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him”: God gave the revelation to Christ, “to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass.” That is why in the scriptures God showed Christ certain things, and Christ comes to us telling us thus saith the Lord.

What Christ did: “he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John.” His angel, meaning the angels belong to Christ. God showed it to Christ, Christ showed it unto the angel, and the angel showed it unto his servants. That is the divine order.

“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending.” This is the angel saying this, speaking on the behalf of Christ. When you read in Revelation, that is an angel speaking, but he is speaking on the behalf of Christ.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

points: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone. You see that? Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die. Guess what? That corn of wheat is you. You must fall to the ground and die. What does that mean? You have got to kill that old man.
But if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit. Once you kill that old man, you bring forth much fruit.
He that loveth his life shall lose it. You see that? If you love that old life, you have got to lose it in order to get the eternal life.
And he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal. If you hate this life, and you do the things to get the eternal life, you are going to be good according to the scriptures.

If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be. Where Christ is, that is where his servant is going to be. That is what we want. We want to get the kingdom of heaven. We want to be where Christ is.

“For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle.” The Pharisees were losing their following: “behold, the world is gone after him.” The world there is the Jews who went after Christ because of Lazarus.

“And there were certain Greeks among them that came up to worship at the feast”. Why are there Greeks among the Jews, worshipping at the feast? Who are these Greeks? The margin of the King James sends you to John 7:35, where the Greeks are the dispersed.

In the Greek the word is Hellen, number 1672. A Greek by nationality, but in a wider sense all nations, not Jews, who made the language, customs and learning of the Greeks their own, and the primary reference is to a difference of religion and worship. So a Greek was not only one born Greek: whoever took up the religion and worship of the Greeks became a Greek.

These Greeks were our own people, scattered abroad and Hellenized, who had come back to keep the customs of their forefathers, called proselytes. You cannot tell me the Greeks of John 12:20 are actual Gentiles.

“While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.” Though he had done so many miracles before them, they did not believe Christ.
Pay attention to what he is saying: “Lord, who hath believed our report?” They don’t want to believe us. “And to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

“Therefore they could not believe”, because of what Isaiah said again: “He hath blinded their eyes”, and hardened their hearts, “that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.” This is what the Lord did: he blinded our people’s eyes and their hearts, so that they can’t see and understand. The I that should heal them is Christ.

“These things said” Isaiah, “when he saw his glory, and spake of him.” He saw Christ’s glory, and he spoke of Christ. These scriptures, brothers, are on another level. Isaiah saw Christ and saw his glory; he saw the Lord from heaven. They keep playing with us like we don’t know what we are talking about, but right through the Bible it is Christ; right through the Bible it is him.

“Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.” They heard a voice coming from heaven. A lot of times people read this and answer that it was God speaking. No: nobody ever heard God’s voice.
Do you understand what a messenger is? The word angel means messenger. Angels speak on the behalf of God.

“Others said, An angel spake to him.” The angel is speaking, but the angel is speaking on the behalf of the Father: I have glorified it, and will keep glorifying it. No one has ever heard the voice of the Father; it was always Christ, or an angel speaking on the behalf of the Father.
